newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwandan troops break up special Red Cross camp.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan troops break up special Red Cross camp.

text.p: The Rwandan authorities closed down on Monday a Red Cross camp for 350 sick and exhaused Rwandan refugees, a Red Cross spokesman said.

Andrew Hall said that officials saying they were from the Ministry of Rehabilitation ordered the special Red Cross camp inside Unbano camp near the border with Zaire closed and the refugees inside were taken away in trucks.

"They didn't give specific reasons, or (said) only that they wanted the camps around the borders of Rwanda removed," said Hall, spokesman for the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.
He said the 350 sick and vulnerable refugees including the elderly, the disabled and "people in a fairly unstable medical condition" were ushered onto the trucks and driven away.
"There was no physical violence. Sticks were waved around, but they weren't used," he said.

Hall said the Red Cross staff expressed concern about the medical condition of the 350 taken away and the Red Cross was making representations to the Rwandan government over the incident. Unbano camp is the first unofficial camp reached by refugees trekking in from Zaire through the Rwandan town of Gisenyi. It is about four kms (two miles) from the border.
